title: Chemistry — Mission 1: The Stoichiometry Leak
description: A reagent shortage in the school lab has the Friday demo in danger. You have one supply run to figure out exactly how much of each chemical the reaction actually needs.

mika.name: Ms. Mika Tan
mika.description: Has run this reaction a thousand times and can smell a bad ratio.

dev.name: Dev
dev.description: Thinks 'balancing an equation' means keeping the beaker from tipping over.

periodic_table.name: Periodic Table Card
periodic_table.description: Molar masses for every element, right where you need them.

reaction_sheet.name: Reaction Sheet
reaction_sheet.description: The unbalanced equation for Friday's demo.

elements.text: We're short on reagent and I need to know exactly how many moles this reaction actually consumes before I order more.
Can't we just order double of everything to be safe?

options.text: "We should balance the equation first — the mole ratios tell us exactly what we need."
"Just double the order, budget's not my problem."

elements.text: Good, you grabbed the reaction sheet. Let's balance it properly.
Ordering blind wastes the department's whole budget. We need the real ratio.

config.question: For the unbalanced equation N2 + H2 -> NH3, what are the correct coefficients?
config.explanation: Balancing nitrogen and hydrogen atoms on both sides requires N2 + 3H2 -> 2NH3.

config.prompt: Order these steps of a stoichiometry calculation from first to last.

items.text: Apply the mole ratio from the equation
Convert answer moles back to grams

config.prompt: Dev: "Quick, what's the molar mass of water, H2O, in g/mol? Round to the nearest whole number."

elements.text: Exact quantities, under budget. Friday's demo is safe.
We ordered enough, barely. Next time, balance the equation before you order anything.

elements.prompt: The order form is submitted. What now?

options.text: Show Dev how to work a stoichiometry problem start to finish.
Sign off. The order's in — that's enough for today.

elements.text: So the coefficients aren't just for balance, they're literally the ratio of moles reacting. I get it now.

ending.title: Stoichiometry Hero
ending.description: Balanced the equation, ordered exactly what was needed, and taught Dev the whole process.

ending.title: Order Submitted
ending.description: The reagents are ordered. The deeper lesson can wait until tomorrow.
